reason: Conversation 1 correctly identifies E:09 as a heating fault, notes the heater is integrated into the circulation pump assembly, avoids claiming the control board is at fault, and sensibly recommends an engineer. It is brief and does not reach the customer's later questions, but it makes no unsafe or wrong claims. Conversation 2 gives a safety-conscious isolation procedure and the customer's open-circuit result is useful, but it wrongly describes a U-shaped element in the tub bottom, quotes a 20-40 ohm reading and a cheap £30-£40 element, and tells the customer to fit it themselves. The actual fix is a heat pump assembly replacement, which is advanced DIY and costs more. Conversation 2 also suffers repeated truncation, uses euros and dollars at first, and gives misleading part and cost advice, so Conversation 1 is slightly better despite being thinner.
